text:
Priya: quick check-in  we keep seeing downstream services accept tokens minted by our proxy that don't include any claim about the original principal. This makes audits useless. Proposal: exchange tokens must include `orig_fp` (sha256 of original token) and `delegation_chain` shorthand. Thoughts?

Derek: yes. +1 for `orig_fp`. Keep token size small though. `delegation_chain` can be a short list of fingerprints joined by `>`; store full mapping in audit store.

Olga: also add `cred_home` claim indicating whether the credential is org/project scoped. Authz hook can use this to disallow project-only keys acting across projects.

Priya: acceptance criteria suggestion:
- exchanged tokens include `orig_fp` and `dv` (delegation version)
- auth proxy emits `audit:delegation` event with full chain + mapping version
- token TTL for exchanged tokens <= 60s by default

Derek: rollout: implement exchange token claim in proxy, shadow-mode in staging for 1 week, then opt-in per-service. Add metric `missing_orig_fp_count`.

Olga: threat note: ensure `orig_fp` cannot be forged by clients. Only set by trusted proxy when issuing exchange token.

infra-bot: NOTE: audit pipeline ingestion at 75% capacity. Consider sampling non-critical events.

sec-bot: POLICY-CANDIDATE: SVC-DELEG-EXCH-1 (Exchanged tokens must include orig_fp and dv). Filing for review.

Priya: I'll open the PR for proxy changes and a small schema for the audit event. Tagging Derek/Olga when ready. Thanks!
